prompt: What alcohol forms from acid-catalyzed hydration of (R)-4-methyl-1-hexene, CH2=CHCH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3?

choices.text: 4-Methyl-2-hexanol
4-Methyl-1-hexanol
choices.why: That is the non-Markovnikov alcohol. Acid-catalyzed hydration goes through the carbocation at carbon 2.

choices.text: 5-Methyl-2-hexanol
choices.why: That has the methyl branch on a different carbon. Hydration doesn't change the carbon skeleton.

choices.text: 4-Methyl-1,2-hexanediol
choices.why: Hydration adds only one −OH group.

explanation: Protonation gives the secondary carbocation at carbon 2, which reacts with water, giving 4-methyl-2-hexanol.

prompt: How many chirality centers does 4-methyl-2-hexanol, CH3CH(OH)CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3, have?
explanation: Carbon 2 (H, OH, CH3 and the rest of the chain) and carbon 4 (H, CH3, CH2CH3 and the rest of the chain) each carry four different groups, so the molecule has two chirality centers.

prompt: How many stereoisomers are possible for 4-methyl-2-hexanol?
explanation: With two chirality centers there are 2^2 = 4 possible stereoisomers: (2R,4R), (2S,4S), (2R,4S) and (2S,4R).

prompt: In the acid-catalyzed hydration of (R)-4-methyl-1-hexene, what is the configuration at carbon 4 of the product?

choices.text: R, because that chirality center is unaffected by the reaction
S, because adding water inverts the existing chirality center
choices.why: Carbon 4 isn't involved in the reaction, so its configuration doesn't change.

choices.text: A 50:50 mixture of R and S, since the cation is planar
choices.why: Carbon 4's configuration was set in the starting material and stays the same.

choices.text: None, because carbon 4 is no longer a chirality center
choices.why: Carbon 4 still carries H, CH3, CH2CH3 and the chain toward carbon 2: four different groups.

explanation: Carbon 4 has the R configuration in the starting material and is unaffected by the reaction, so it remains R in the product, assuming the relative rankings of its four groups are not changed.

prompt: The section says carbon 4 stays R when (R)-4-methyl-1-hexene is hydrated. What assumption does this rely on?

choices.text: That the rankings of the four groups on carbon 4 don't change
That the carbocation intermediate forms at carbon 4
choices.why: The carbocation forms at carbon 2; carbon 4 isn't involved.

choices.text: That water adds equally to both faces of the carbocation
choices.why: That would concern carbon 2, not carbon 4.

choices.text: That the reaction is run in a chiral environment
choices.why: No chiral environment is needed; carbon 4 simply isn't touched by the reaction.

explanation: Because carbon 4 is not affected by the reaction, its spatial arrangement doesn't change. Its R label stays the same as long as the rankings of its four attached groups are not changed by the reaction.

prompt: Why doesn't the carbocation from (R)-4-methyl-1-hexene react equally with water from its top and bottom faces?

choices.text: It is chiral, with no plane of symmetry, so one face is more accessible
It is planar and achiral, so its top and bottom faces are identical
choices.why: Then the faces would react equally. The chirality center at carbon 4 makes this cation chiral.

choices.text: Its positive carbon is sp3-hybridized, so it isn't planar at all
choices.why: The positive carbon is still sp2 and planar; the difference comes from the chirality center at carbon 4.

choices.text: A bridging bromine atom blocks one face, as in a bromonium ion
choices.why: No halogen is involved. One face is more accessible for steric reasons because the cation is chiral.

explanation: The carbocation is chiral because of the chirality center at carbon 4 and has no plane of symmetry. One face is likely a bit more accessible for steric reasons, so R and S configurations at carbon 2 form in a ratio other than 50:50.

prompt: Which products form from acid-catalyzed hydration of (R)-4-methyl-1-hexene?

choices.text: (2R,4R)- and (2S,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, in unequal amounts
(2R,4R)- and (2S,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, in a 50:50 ratio
choices.why: The chiral carbocation doesn't react equally from both faces, so the amounts are unequal.

choices.text: (2R,4R)- and (2S,4S)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, in equal amounts
choices.why: Carbon 4 stays R; the reaction doesn't change it.

choices.text: Only (2R,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol
choices.why: Water reacts from both faces, just not equally, so both configurations at carbon 2 form.

explanation: Carbon 4 remains R, and the new center at carbon 2 forms as both R and S in unequal amounts. The products, (2R,4R)- and (2S,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, are diastereomers.

prompt: What is the relationship between (2R,4R)- and (2S,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol?

choices.text: They are diastereomers
They are enantiomers
choices.why: Enantiomers have opposite configurations at every chirality center; these differ only at carbon 2.

choices.text: They are identical
choices.why: They differ in configuration at carbon 2.

choices.text: They are constitutional isomers
choices.why: Their atoms are connected the same way; they differ only in the arrangement at carbon 2.

explanation: These two stereoisomers have the same configuration at carbon 4 and opposite configurations at carbon 2, so they are not mirror images: they are diastereomers.

prompt: Is the product mixture from hydration of a single enantiomer, (R)-4-methyl-1-hexene, optically active?

choices.text: Yes, because an optically active reactant gives optically active products
No, because a new chirality center always forms as a racemic mixture
choices.why: That rule applies to achiral reactants. With a chiral reactant, the products are diastereomers in unequal amounts.

choices.text: No, because the two products are enantiomers whose rotations cancel
choices.why: The products are diastereomers, not enantiomers.

choices.text: Yes, but only because carbon 2 forms entirely as R
choices.why: Carbon 2 forms as both R and S. The mixture is optically active because the reactant was a single enantiomer.

explanation: If the chiral reactant is optically active because only one enantiomer is used rather than a racemic mixture, the products are also optically active. Both products here have carbon 4 in the R configuration.

prompt: What is the general rule when a chiral reactant forms a new chirality center?

choices.text: It gives unequal amounts of diastereomeric products
It always gives a racemic mixture of enantiomers
choices.why: That is the rule for achiral reactants.

choices.text: It gives equal amounts of diastereomeric products
choices.why: The chiral reactant's two faces are not equivalent, so the amounts are unequal.

choices.text: It gives a single stereoisomer as the only product
choices.why: Both configurations at the new center form, though in unequal amounts.

explanation: As a general rule, the formation of a new chirality center by a chiral reactant leads to unequal amounts of diastereomeric products. If the reactant is a single enantiomer, the products are optically active too.

prompt: What results from acid-catalyzed hydration of racemic (±)-4-methyl-1-hexene?

choices.text: An optically inactive, non-50:50 mixture of two racemic pairs
An optically active mixture of (2R,4R)- and (2S,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol
choices.why: That is the result from the pure R enantiomer. The S enantiomer in the racemic reactant gives the mirror-image products.

choices.text: A single racemic pair of 4-methyl-2-hexanol and nothing else
choices.why: Each enantiomer of the alkene gives two diastereomers, so two racemic pairs form.

choices.text: Equal amounts of all four stereoisomers of 4-methyl-2-hexanol
choices.why: The diastereomers form in unequal amounts, because each chiral carbocation reacts unequally from its two faces.

explanation: The (R) enantiomer gives (2R,4R) and (2S,4R) in unequal amounts; the (S) enantiomer gives their mirror images, (2S,4S) and (2R,4S), in the same ratio. The result is two racemic pairs, (2R,4R)+(2S,4S) and (2R,4S)+(2S,4R), in non-50:50 amounts, and the mixture is optically inactive.

prompt: How many stereoisomers of 4-methyl-2-hexanol form when racemic (±)-4-methyl-1-hexene undergoes acid-catalyzed hydration?
explanation: Each enantiomer of the alkene gives two diastereomers, and together they make two racemic pairs, (2R,4R)+(2S,4S) and (2R,4S)+(2S,4R): all 4 stereoisomers.

prompt: What can you say about the products of acid-catalyzed hydration of 4-methylcyclopentene?

choices.text: They are two racemic pairs of 3-methylcyclopentanol, formed in a non-50:50 ratio
They are a single racemic pair of 3-methylcyclopentanol, in a 50:50 ratio
choices.why: The new chirality center can form with either configuration relative to the methyl-bearing carbon, giving two diastereomeric pairs.

choices.text: They are two racemic pairs of 3-methylcyclopentanol in exactly equal amounts
choices.why: The two pairs are diastereomers of each other, and they form in unequal amounts.

choices.text: They are a single, optically active enantiomer of 3-methylcyclopentanol
choices.why: No chiral environment is present, so enantiomers form in equal amounts.

explanation: Hydration gives 3-methylcyclopentanol, with chirality centers at carbons 1 and 3. The products are a non-50:50 mixture of two racemic pairs: (1S,3R)+(1R,3S) and (1S,3S)+(1R,3R).

prompt: How many stereoisomers of 3-methylcyclopentanol form in the acid-catalyzed hydration of 4-methylcyclopentene?
explanation: The products are two racemic pairs, (1S,3R)+(1R,3S) and (1S,3S)+(1R,3R), formed in a non-50:50 ratio: 4 stereoisomers in all.

prompt: What products would form from acid-catalyzed hydration of (S)-4-methyl-1-hexene?

choices.text: (2R,4S)- and (2S,4S)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, in unequal amounts
(2R,4R)- and (2S,4R)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, in unequal amounts
choices.why: Carbon 4 keeps the configuration of the starting material, which is S here.

choices.text: (2R,4S)- and (2S,4S)-4-methyl-2-hexanol, in a 50:50 ratio
choices.why: The chiral carbocation reacts unequally from its two faces.

choices.text: Only (2S,4S)-4-methyl-2-hexanol
choices.why: Both configurations at carbon 2 form, in unequal amounts.

explanation: Carbon 4 is unaffected and remains S (assuming the group rankings don't change). The new center at carbon 2 forms as both R and S in unequal amounts, giving the diastereomers (2R,4S) and (2S,4S): the mirror images of the products from the (R) alkene.
